Newly-formed Invest 93W is a very weak embedded monsoon disturbance
well west of the Marianas, which is expected to induce low-end
scattered showers tonight. Mostly dry conditions will return 
thereafter as winds remain light, followed by a monsoon surge 
developing across the region beginning this weekend. Said monsoon
surge will introduce southwesterly to westerly winds and a wet 
pattern coming into next week, with winds likely to keep increasing
as Typhoon Dolphin (12W) moves between the far northern CNMI and 
Wake Island.

Marine...
Light easterlies will slowly turn to the south and increase over
the next few days, becoming straight west come Friday night as a
monsoon regime ensues. Winds will then turn west on Friday and 
gradually increase through the weekend. Combined seas of 3 to 4 
feet are expected to continue through Thursday, followed by the 
arrival of an easterly swell generated by distant Typhoon Dolphin 
and strengthening westerly swells. By the weekend, the aforementioned
monsoonal regime is likely to introduce sea conditions hazardous 
to small craft. A low risk of rip currents is expected along all reefs
of the Marianas through Thursday, to then become moderate along north
and east facing reefs as an easterly swell generated by distant 
Typhoon Dolphin (12W) arrives. Surf will continue to increase along
all reefs for much of the week as the easterly swell and newly 
developing westerly swells increase, with a chance for hazardous surf 
to form by the end of the week.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon Dolphin has strengthened significantly since yesterday, with
current winds of 140 mph, adding 70 mph to it's maximum winds since
yesterday's Tropical Weather Discussion. Dolphin is centered near 
14.3N 168.7E, moving west-northwest at 10 mph. Dolphin is expected 
to weaken slightly over the next 12 hours due to entering a region of
slightly stronger vertical wind shear between 500 and 300 mb. 
Satellite trends do show that Dolphin has halted it's intense 
strengthening, with cooling temps in the eye and slight warming in 
the eyewall. These conditions are also indicative of an eyewall 
replacement cycle, which would also account for little change to 
slight weakening as it goes through this cycle. A 28/1418Z AMSR2 pass
also helps support this scenario, showing a tiny inner core with a 
more intense outer spiral band. Overall, Dolphin looks to begin to 
intensify again late tonight, possibly becoming a Super Typhoon 
Thursday night or Friday. Dolphin is expected to make a slight turn 
toward the northwest over the next 12 to 24 hours, with little change
in speed. Dolphin looks to pass south of Wake Island some time 
Thursday, and if strengthening resumes, could bring damaging wind and
seas along with torrential rain to Wake Island. Residents of Wake 
Island should continue to monitor the progress of Typhoon Dolphin 
closely.

For more information on TY Dolphin, please refer to bulletins issued
by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) under WMO header WTPN31 
PGTW and by the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 
PGUM.

A weak circulation, JTWC's Invest 94W, is centered near 12.4N 
140.5E. Invest 94W is currently rated sub-low, meaning little or no 
development is expected over the next few days. 94W is not expected 
to strengthen much, if at all, as it continues to move slowly W over 
the next few days. 94W is not expected to directly impact Palau or 
Yap State, however, it could enhance monsoon flow, resulting in a 
monsoon surge over the next day or two. Invest 94W will be monitored 
closely over the coming days for any changes to these expectations.

Eastern Micronesia...
The monsoon trough continues to produce bands of convection across
portions of eastern Micronesia. Unfortunately, it's becoming more
difficult to identify exactly where the flare ups will occur.
Therefore, an overall unsettled forecast continues, with POPs
(Probability of Precipitation) remaining in the 30 to 50 percent
range with the trough. Majuro is currently in a dry slot, however, 
this is not expected to remain the case through the night. 
Therefore, decided to bring scattered showers into Majuro later this 
evening. For Kosrae, the island is found along the far southeast 
edge of the convection, but this is also expected to increase through
the evening. Overall, not much of a change as the monsoon trough 
will be pulled a bit farther north as TY Dolphin progresses, allowing
a drier pattern to move into Pohnpei and Kosrae for the weekend. The
monsoon trough will eventually break away from Dolphin and 
reestablish a bit farther south, but looks to continue to influence 
the Marshalls into next week.
